title: Before all of them, the people of Nuh went the same way.
subtitle: The oldest sign in the list
then: The list of signs ends by going back to the first: {trap}the people of Nuh, before them all.{/trap} The tafsir says Allah destroyed them before Pharaoh, Aad and Thamud. They were a people who {trap}rebelled against what they were told.{/trap}
now: You keep making the same mistake in different jobs, different friendships, different cities. You think each one is a new story. {idea}Look at the pattern, not the scenery.{/idea}
old: Every situation I end up in is different.
new: When the same ending repeats, the cause is usually the same choice.
try: Write down one pattern that keeps repeating in your life. Name the choice behind it.

title: The sky was built with strength and is still being widened.
subtitle: Look up from the ruins
then: After the ruined nations, the surah looks up. The tafsir says Allah made the sky {idea}a high roof, protected from falling{/idea}, built with strength, and {reward}made it vast without pillars to support it.{/reward} It is a proof of His Oneness.
now: You walk to the car with your eyes on your phone. Above you is a roof with no pillars that has not fallen once in your life. {idea}Look up for ten seconds.{/idea} The One who holds that up can hold your day.
new: The sky is a daily proof that Allah holds what I cannot.
try: Step outside tonight, look up for one full minute, and say SubhanAllah.

title: The earth was spread out like a bed for you.
subtitle: The ground as a gift
then: The tafsir explains that Allah {reward}made the earth a resting place for the created{/reward} and spread it for its inhabitants. He praises Himself: {idea}how excellent a spreader!{/idea} The sky above, the ground below, both point to one Maker.
now: You pay rent or a mortgage and feel you earned the ground you stand on. But the floor under the floor, the soil, water and air, was ready before you were born. {reward}You walked into a prepared room.{/reward}
old: I worked for every bit of ground I have.
new: The ground itself was prepared for me before I did anything.
try: Before sleeping tonight, thank Allah by name for one thing about the place you live.

title: Everything comes in pairs, so you remember the One.
subtitle: Pairs point to the One without a pair

row.title: only the Creator has no pair

then: The tafsir lists the pairs: heaven and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, {idea}faith and disbelief, misery and happiness, Paradise and Fire.{/idea} All of it so that {reward}you remember the Creator is One.{/reward}
now: Your phone and its charger. Your left hand and your right. Morning coffee and evening tiredness. {idea}Everything you own needs a partner to work.{/idea} The One who made them all needs nothing.
old: Pairs are just how things happen to be.
new: Everything needing another reminds me that Allah alone needs no one.
try: Notice three pairs around you today and, for each, say Allah is One.

title: Run toward Allah, not away from Him.
subtitle: Where to go when you are afraid
then: After the signs in the sky, the earth and the pairs, the call comes: {reward}flee to Allah.{/reward} The tafsir explains it as {idea}seek shelter with Him and trust in Him in all of your affairs.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ is a clear warner from Him.
now: Bad news hits and you run: to the fridge, to scrolling, to blaming, to staying in bed. {idea}The verse points you the other way.{/idea} Run to the One who can actually carry it.
old: When things go wrong, I escape into anything that numbs it.
new: The safest place to run when afraid is toward Allah.
try: Next time you feel the urge to escape, pause and make wudu or say one dua first.

title: Do not put anything beside Allah.
subtitle: The warning repeated, with a new edge
then: The verse before said flee to Allah. This one closes the side door: {trap}do not set up another god with Him.{/trap} The tafsir says do not associate partners with Him. {idea}The same words, I am a clear warner, repeat to drive it home.{/idea}
now: You pray, and also keep a lucky charm, a horoscope app, a quiet belief that your boss really decides your fate. {trap}Small partners creep in.{/trap} {idea}Running to Allah means running to Him alone.{/idea}
old: Trusting Allah and trusting other things too seems harmless.
new: Real shelter in Allah has no partner standing beside Him.
try: Identify one thing you treat as if it controls your fate. Remind yourself today that only Allah does.

title: Every messenger heard the same insult.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: I must be doing it wrong

then: The tafsir says {idea}Allah comforts His Prophet ﷺ{/idea} here. The people of Makkah were calling him names. Allah tells him: the disbelievers of old {trap}used the same words with their messengers.{/trap} Pharaoh said them to Musa earlier in this very surah.
now: You start praying at work, or stop drinking, or wear what you believe in. Someone calls you extreme, or weird. {idea}You are not the first.{/idea} The insult is old, and so is the path you are on.
old: If people mock me for doing right, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Mockery for doing right is an old road, walked by every messenger.
try: If someone teases you for your faith this week, answer once, kindly, and let it go.

title: They never met, yet they said the same thing.
subtitle: Same hearts, same words
then: Allah asks: {idea}did the people of the past teach these words to the people of the present?{/idea} The answer is no. The tafsir says they are tyrannical people {trap}whose hearts are the same{/trap}, so they say the same.
now: You catch yourself saying exactly what your father said when he was angry, word for word, though you swore you never would. {idea}The words follow the heart.{/idea} Change what is inside and the words change.
old: My words just come out; they do not mean much.
new: What I say repeatedly shows me what my heart has become.
try: Notice one phrase you say often when frustrated. Ask what feeling sits under it.

title: Turn away from them. You are not to blame.
subtitle: Letting go of what is not yours
then: The tafsir says: {idea}O Muhammad ﷺ, turn away from the Quraysh idolators.{/idea} Allah adds, {reward}We blame you not if you turn away from them.{/reward} He had conveyed the message clearly. Their refusal was not his failure.
now: You keep sending the long message, trying again with the relative who will not listen. You lie awake replaying it. {reward}You are not blamed for their no.{/reward} Say it well, then rest.
old: If someone does not change, it is because I failed them.
new: My job is to speak kindly and clearly. Their answer belongs to them.
try: Think of one person you keep trying to fix. Make dua for them and let the next argument go.

title: Keep reminding. Believing hearts benefit.
subtitle: Turning away is not going silent
then: Right after turn away comes {idea}and remind.{/idea} The tafsir explains: {reward}only the believing hearts benefit from being reminded.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ was not to stop teaching, only to stop chasing those set on refusing.
now: You stopped sharing anything about faith because one cousin always mocks it. But your sister reads every word, and your friend quietly started praying. {reward}Remind for them.{/reward}
old: If some people mock reminders, I should stop giving them.
new: Reminders are for hearts ready to hear. Those hearts are worth it.
try: Share one short, kind reminder today with someone you know is open to it.

title: You were made to worship Him. That is the point.
subtitle: The reason behind everything
then: The tafsir says Allah created them {idea}so that they worship Him alone{/idea}, not that He needs them. It quotes a hadith: {reward}busy yourself in worship and I will fill your chest with riches{/reward}, otherwise the chest fills with distraction.
now: You fill the day with tabs, tasks, and errands, and at night feel empty and busy at once. {idea}The verse names what you were made for.{/idea} Even work, kindness, and rest can be worship when done for Him.
old: Worship is one part of life, squeezed in when I have time.
new: Worship is the reason for my life, and it can run through all of it.
try: Pick one ordinary task today and do it with the intention of pleasing Allah.

title: He wants no food or income from you.
subtitle: A master unlike any other
then: Human masters keep servants so the servants can feed and enrich them. Allah says He wants {idea}no provision from them{/idea} and does not ask to be fed. The tafsir says {reward}they are in need of Him in all conditions{/reward}, not the other way.
now: Your boss needs your hours. Your landlord needs your rent. Even friends sometimes need something back. {idea}Allah asks for your worship and gains nothing from it.{/idea} Every bit of it returns to you.
old: Everyone who asks something of me wants to get something.
new: Allah asks of me only what benefits me. He needs nothing.
try: During your next prayer, remind yourself once that this is for your benefit, not His.

title: Allah is the Provider, strong and firm.
subtitle: Who actually puts food on your table
then: Having said He needs nothing, Allah says what He is: {reward}the All-Provider, Owner of power, the Most Strong.{/reward} The tafsir mentions that the Prophet ﷺ taught these words. {idea}He alone is their Creator and Provider.{/idea}
now: Payday is late, the contract ends, a client disappears. Your stomach drops. {idea}The company was only a channel.{/idea} {reward}The Provider is still the Provider.{/reward}
old: My income depends on my employer.
new: My employer is a door. The Provider is Allah, and He is never weak.
try: When you next check your bank balance, say Ya Razzaq once, and thank Him for today.

title: Their share is coming, so do not ask it to hurry.
subtitle: The same portion as those before
then: The deniers mocked: if punishment is real, bring it now. The tafsir says they will {trap}receive their due share{/trap}, like the nations already described, and {idea}let them not ask that it be rushed, for it will surely come.{/idea}
now: You do something wrong and nothing happens, so you dare it again, almost testing whether anything ever will. {idea}The quiet is not a verdict.{/idea} It is time given to turn back.
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, it probably never will.
new: Delay is a mercy to use, not proof that nothing is coming.
try: Take one wrong you have gotten away with and quietly put it right, or ask Allah's forgiveness for it.

title: The promised Day is coming. Be ready for it.
subtitle: How the surah ends

row.title: prepared
sub: what the surah began with: it is true

then: The surah opened with oaths that the promise is true and the Judgment will happen. It closes with {trap}woe to those who disbelieve{/trap} from their promised Day. The tafsir says this is {idea}the Day of Resurrection.{/idea}
now: You plan for the exam, the wedding, retirement, all days you are not even sure you will see. {idea}One Day is certain.{/idea} {reward}A little preparing for it today makes it a day to look forward to.{/reward}
old: The Day of Judgment is far away and abstract.
new: It is the one appointment I am sure to keep, so I can prepare for it now.
try: Do one deed today you would be glad to find on that Day: a prayer on time, a call to a parent, a gift.
